project.name: Little CMS
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace under `gt_results/arvo_42227/_work/src/lcms` is currently checked out at parent commit `1c667a762c4272ec970a2dd6f945836c52f35720`, but the exact vulnerable source for this trace was read from commit object `b949a3840e0ae8ae05898fb96187b0d123693d92` in that local `.git`. Its `src/cmscgats.c` lines match the staged `patch.diff` and saved ASan frames, and commit `32d19328855dd599bf7f15dcfd5fafd6f87fb0d5` is the direct fix adding `|| it8->ch == 0` to the quoted-string loop.

bug_description.original: An overflow condition occurs when processing an ill-formed CGATS file.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / staged `patch.diff` / staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `reproduction_report.json` / vulnerable commit object `b949a3840e0ae8ae05898fb96187b0d123693d92` in the staged ARVO workspace
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 10-byte ASCII/CR file `20 20 20 20 0d 3f 22 22 20 22`, i.e. a blank first line followed by `?"" "` with no closing quote for the final token. `cmsIT8LoadFromMem()` copies those bytes into `MemoryBlock` and appends `MemoryBlock[len] = 0`, so the parser has a synthetic NUL immediately after the trailing quote. After `ReadType()` consumes the blank first line, `HeaderSection()` accepts `?` as a non-strict header property name, parses `""` as its first empty string value, and then treats the remaining lone `"` as the start of a second quoted value. In vulnerable commit `b949a3840e0ae8ae05898fb96187b0d123693d92`, `InStringSymbol()` breaks only on CR or LF, not on `it8->ch == 0`, so once `NextCh()` reaches the appended NUL it keeps appending NUL bytes forever and repeatedly grows `it8->str`. The failing growth calls `memcpy(new_ptr, s->begin, s->len)` with `s->len = 102399999`, matching the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow` WRITE in `StringAppend()`. Commit `32d19328855dd599bf7f15dcfd5fafd6f87fb0d5` fixes this exact path by adding `|| it8->ch == 0` to the loop guard.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled CGATS bytes into the parser's in-memory buffer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 10-byte witness `20 20 20 20 0d 3f 22 22 20 22`. This statement copies those bytes from `Ptr,len` into `it8->MemoryBlock`; the next statement appends the sentinel NUL that later becomes the EOF character inside the unterminated second quoted string.

sink.description: The string-growth copy uses the attacker-amplified string length as the byte count. ASan reports this exact call as a `global-buffer-overflow` WRITE of 102399999 bytes.

root_cause.description: The quoted-string loop stops on CR or LF but not on EOF. When the second quoted token reaches the appended NUL, `it8->ch == 0` falls through to `StringAppend()` instead of terminating, so the parser appends NUL forever.
root_cause.note: The direct fix changes this guard to `if (it8->ch == '\n' || it8->ch == '\r' || it8->ch == 0) break;`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged build is on the non-strict header path, so the second-line identifier `?` is admitted as a property name instead of being rejected.
parser_admitted.note: Successful reproduction proves the `#else` branch is active here: after the blank first line, `VarName` is `?`, `AddAvailableProperty()` creates a header key for it, and the parser proceeds to consume the following quoted tokens as its values.

tainted_value_origin.description: Loads the current character from the attacker-controlled in-memory CGATS buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing second quoted token, `it8->Source` has advanced to `it8->MemoryBlock[len]`, the sentinel NUL appended after the staged bytes `20 20 20 20 0d 3f 22 22 20 22`. This statement therefore materializes `it8->ch = 0`, the EOF value that should terminate the string loop but does not in the vulnerable source.
tainted_value_origin.note: `NextCh()` only increments `it8->Source` when the loaded byte is nonzero, so repeated calls at EOF keep returning the same `0` byte.

coarse_trace.summary: Copies the staged 10-byte ill-formed CGATS witness into `MemoryBlock` and appends a NUL sentinel immediately after the trailing quote.
Treats the first line as blank, then continues into ordinary header parsing on the second line.
Accepts `?` as a header property name, consumes `""` as its first value, and leaves a trailing unmatched `"` to be parsed as the next token.
The second quoted-string parse reaches the appended EOF NUL immediately after the opening quote, but the vulnerable loop does not stop on `it8->ch == 0`.
Repeated EOF appends inflate the string length until the resize path calls `memcpy(new_ptr, s->begin, s->len)` and crashes.

fine_trace.note: Copies the staged 10-byte witness `20 20 20 20 0d 3f 22 22 20 22` into parser-owned memory. Interpreted by later parsing, those bytes form a blank first line followed by `?"" "`.
Appends a synthetic NUL immediately after the trailing quote. Because the final token has no closing delimiter, this sentinel becomes the first character seen inside the second quoted-string parse.

After `ReadType()` and `SkipEOLN()` consume the blank first line, the second-line identifier has become `VarName = "?"`. Because the staged build is on the non-strict `#else` path, `HeaderSection()` admits `?` as a property name and continues to parse following tokens as its values instead of rejecting the file.

When `HeaderSection()` asks for the first value of property `?`, the next token is `""`. `StringClear()` resets the string buffer, `NextCh()` immediately sees the closing quote, so the loop body is skipped and the call returns an empty `SSTRING`, advancing `it8->ch` to the separator space before the final lone quote.

After storing `? = ""`, `HeaderSection()` calls `InSymbol()` again. `InSymbol()` skips the separator space, sees the remaining lone `"`, and dispatches a second time to `InStringSymbol()` even though no closing quote remains in the buffer.

This second `InStringSymbol()` invocation has just cleared `it8->str`, so the string length starts at 0. After consuming the opening quote, `NextCh()` reads the sentinel from step 2 and materializes `it8->ch = 0` because the file ended immediately after that quote.

With `it8->ch == 0`, the quoted-string loop still enters the `else` branch because the vulnerable guard checks only CR and LF. `StringAppend()` therefore appends a NUL byte instead of terminating at EOF, and the paired `NextCh()` call re-reads the same zero byte, creating an endless append loop. The fix adds `|| it8->ch == 0` to this guard.

Each pass through the buggy EOF loop appends one more NUL and increments `it8->str->len` from 0 upward. Because the loop never sees a closing quote or advances past EOF, this repetition drives `s->len` all the way to 102399999, the copy size recorded by ASan at the failing growth.

Once the repeated NUL appends make `s->len + 1` reach the current capacity, `StringAppend()` takes its growth branch. At the failing iteration, the loop has driven `s->len` to 102399999 and `s->max` to 102400000, so this branch raises `s->max` to 1024000000 and requests a new destination buffer before copying the old contents.
The resize copy uses the attacker-amplified `s->len` as the `memcpy()` byte count. The saved ASan trace reports this exact call as a `global-buffer-overflow` WRITE of 102399999 bytes.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42227 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` in `StringAppend`.

format.name: ill-formed CGATS header with a trailing unmatched quote
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 10-byte ASCII/CR file `20 20 20 20 0d 3f 22 22 20 22`. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to this layout: the first four spaces and `\r` form an empty first line; `?` is admitted as a header identifier in the staged non-strict parser; the next `""` becomes that property's first empty string value; the separating space is skipped; and the final lone `"` starts a second quoted value that reaches `MemoryBlock[len] = 0` immediately because no closing quote exists. The staged artifacts justify this exact unmatched-quote witness, not a broader class beyond a CGATS header token that ends with an opening quote at EOF.
